programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. \nIn this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc:
One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. 
It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. 
For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. 
In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration \"weaponized\" in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.\nThe Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.\nFrom Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows.

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.\n\nIn this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging \"AI tourism\" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programme.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programme.desc:
Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy.

We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations.

One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programme.title: No Power, No AI
programme.desc: Is energy the ultimate bottleneck for artificial intelligence? As compute demand skyrockets, can our power grids keep up? CGTN's Michael Wang moderates a critical panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum on the intersection of AI and energy infrastructure. We'll explore how to align capital investment, infrastructure build-out, and policy frameworks; future-proof energy supply systems to strengthen energy security; and build a more inclusive, sustainable AI-powered energy future. Tune in as global leaders tackle the energy challenge powering the next wave of AI.\n#SummerDavos2026.

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program \"China Untapped: Suzhou\" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou’s high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou’s urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou’s industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: Young Shaolin master
programme.desc: Xu Haican is a kung fu practitioner at the Quanzhou Shaolin Temple in Fujian. The 12-year-old boy is now an expert with the sword, the nine-section chain whip, and the monkey stick after just two years of training. Xu said these weapons give him both confidence and discipline, as he must wield them safely in practice. The young Shaolin master said he hopes to learn more from his masters and carry forward the Chinese martial art.

programme.title: The Datong Motorcycle Diaries

programme.title: Valentine’s for the Pumi People
programme.desc: In this episode, we record the grand celebration of the traditional Pumi Valentine's Day in Luoguqing, Lanping County, Yunnan Province. Every year, on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, young men and women from the local community gather on the vast meadows of Luoguqing to take part in singing and dancing activities in pursuit of marriage. During the program, the host interacts with local people of the Pumi and other ethnic groups, showcasing the traditional plateau lifestyle of the Pumi people, their distinctive firepit culture, as well as the community’s brand-new look in the new era. All these scenes unfold against the lively backdrop of the Valentine’s Day activities, fostering a warm atmosphere of ethnic solidarity.

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film \"Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon\".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2
programme.desc: In Huangshan, Anhui Province, the hosts enjoy a cup of Queen Elizabeth II's favorite tea, as well as the oldest green tea to be exported Europe, and get hands on with quirky local delicacies ranging from \"word candy\" and tofu made of leaves, to the downright funky flavors of hairy tofu and stinky mandarin fish.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise.\nKleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 3
programme.desc: Join us in Nanjing’s bustling old quarter, where you can try on silk dresses worth their weight in gold, and see how traditional handicrafts have been given modern twists. We’ll feast on street snacks and local delicacies by the old Confucian Temple, before taking a pleasure cruise along Nanjing’s mother river to round off our exploration of this vibrant and historic city.

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game \"Sifu\" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to \"eat porridge at night\.

programme.title: China Popcast: All you need to know for traveling in China this summer
programme.desc: Traveling in China for the first time can be a little easier if you know a few things beforehand. In this episode of China Popcast, we tell you which maps to use, how to pay for things, offer advice on how to book tickets for major attractions, share information on China's current travel visa policies and more. Our guests Chen Hongpeng, a Beijing-based tour guide, and CGTN China Travel host Jack Klumpp join the show to give you expert tips for your China trip this summer. And new China Popcast host Min Rui gets the show going with quickfire questions on the \"dos and don'ts.\.

programme.title: Brian Linden: Take me home, country roads
programme.desc: \"Since first arriving in China in 1984, Brian Linden has built a bond with the country that now spans more than four decades. For over 20 years, he has been rooted in Xizhou, a historic town in Yunnan. Drawn by Eastern culture, he arrived as an outsider but gradually became a dedicated rural builder.\nThough he has traveled to more than 120 countries, Linden ultimately chose to settle in rural southwest China. What inspired him to stay, and what China story does he hope to share with the world? Follow Linden’s journey as we explore his life in rural China.\.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Nature’s Bounty
programme.desc: In this episode, we start from hiking up volcanoes in Datong. There is a large volcanic cluster with over 30 cones. Then we come to the Hanging Temple – a 1,500-year-old monastery clutching at a cliff of Mount Hengshan. Join us for an adrenaline-pumping adventure.

programme.title: Valentine's with the Snake King
programme.desc: Every year on Qixi Festival (Chinese Valentine's Day), the town of Zhanghu in Nanping, Fujian Province hosts a folk custom event: the Snake King Parade. Local residents carry the statue of the Snake King from the temple, along with specially prepared pythons, and parade through the streets and alleys. Wherever the procession passes, residents and shopkeepers greet them with firecrackers and burn incense to pray, hoping to receive the unique blessing of the Snake King. This distinctive folk activity is rarely seen elsewhere across China. Taking this event as its highlight, the episode leads audiences on a deep dive into the towns and villages of northern Fujian, delivering a highly engaging and visually appealing viewing experience.

programme.title: A Magic Chinese New Year
programme.desc: During the Year‑of‑the‑Ox Spring Festival, we visited Gubei Water Town in Miyun District, Beijing. Join host He Tianran to experience an authentic northern‑style Spring Festival. We will paste paper lanterns, cut paper‑cut window decorations, watch sugar‑blowing craftsmanship and release sky lanterns. Let us embrace this blessed Year of the Ox together.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game \"Sifu\" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to \"eat porridge at night\.

programme.title: Wild Wonders Ep.4
programme.desc: China's vast land features extraordinary geological diversity and climate zones. Home to 5,000 years of civilization and 1.4 billion people, it sustains the world's second-largest economy while sheltering over 2,000 nature reserves. This documentary spotlights China's natural heritage for tomorrow's possibilities.

programme.title: Taohuawu New Year's Painting
programme.desc: Taohuawu New Year woodblock prints, originating from Suzhou, are iconic symbols of Chinese folk art. These vibrant prints, traditionally displayed during Chinese New Year, depict auspicious scenes, deities, and daily life, embodying wishes for prosperity and happiness. Explore the intricate carving and printing techniques that bring these colorful cultural treasures to life.

programme.title: A Sip of Mount Wuyi
programme.desc: Wuyi rock tea, nurtured in the mineral-rich cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains, is a distinctive oolong embodying a unique \"rock rhyme\" (yan yun)—a taste of nature's harmony. More than a beverage, teas like Da Hong Pao invite mindful appreciation, reflecting centuries of tradition and a philosophy of patience in their complex roasted notes and enduring aftertaste. Discover the terroir, meticulous processing, and the spirit of Chinese tea culture within these exceptional leaves.

programme.desc: Over 3000 years ago, inscriptions were made into the bones of oxen and the undersides of turtle shells for the purpose of divination. programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper

programme.desc: Michael Symon kicks off a new era of Simply Symons from Venice, California, joined by Liz Symon and Olivia “Liv” Annacone Cisic for a laid-back backyard cookout centered around the ultimate burger debate: smash burgers versus classic pub burgers. Michael walks through the techniques behind each style, from selecting the ideal fat ratio for ground beef to achieving the perfect crust on a hot grill and cast iron griddle. Along the way, the trio shares stories about old Symon’s Dinners episodes, Liv’s transition into motherhood, and the realities of filming outdoors with planes overhead, lawn equipment buzzing nearby, and neighborhood life unfolding around them. As Michael builds both burgers with grilled onions, pickles, secret sauce, and different cheeses, the conversation turns into a humorous discussion about condiments, cooking preferences, smash burger myths, and burger nostalgia. Liz keeps the energy going with playful jabs at Michael while also preparing his favorite cocktail, the bourbon-based Paper Plane, complete with Aperol, Amaro, and fresh lemon juice. The episode wraps with a tasting session comparing both burgers side-by-side, with everyone weighing in on which version wins the battle. Between the casual banter, cooking tips, and family-style atmosphere, the episode delivers an easygoing and highly approachable backyard burger feast.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: In this Memorial Day-themed episode of Simply Symons, Michael Symon cooks outdoors with his wife Liz and co-host Olivia Annacone Cisic, preparing grilled shrimp skewers with a honey-soy-orange glaze, a pineapple salsa, and a coconut rice pilaf, while Liz mixes up a frothy pineapple daiquiri with an egg-white twist. The episode opens with playful banter about Olivia's discovery of gray hairs at 33, her upcoming bachelorette party plans, and Michael's gentle ribbing of the trio's early-dinner, early-bedtime lifestyle. Michael walks through his Memorial Day menu, highlighting a coconut rice made with jasmine rice, coconut milk, and a coconut curry lime bone broth from friend Marco Canora's brand Brodo, plus a bright pineapple salsa built with cilantro, scallion, red pepper, jalapeño, honey, and a dashi soy sauce sourced from Santa Monica's McCall's butcher. A lively debate breaks out over rice ratios and rinsing technique, with Liz advocating for a 1:1¾ ratio while Michael sticks to his two-to-one method, and Olivia sharing that she recently cooked jasmine rice for her unwell dog Zeke. Throughout the cooking session, mishaps and humor keep things lively — limes refuse to juice, Liz nearly topples the dashi bottle, and Michael accidentally steps on their dog Min. Discussions range from shrimp varieties and sizing (the U-number system), to the fruity heat of jalapeños and habaneros, to favorite hot sauces including Crystal and the Florida datil-pepper-based Zabs. Liz's honest palate becomes a recurring theme, with Michael crediting her direct, critical feedback as a key ingredient in his culinary success over the years. Liz dry-shakes her egg-white pineapple daiquiri before adding ice for a frothy finish, then adjusts the balance mid-tasting by swirling in extra pineapple juice. The shrimp grill up with beautiful caramelization from the honey glaze, and the coconut rice is finished simply with cilantro and cracked black pepper. During the final tasting, Olivia — a self-described texture-averse pasta lover — bravely tries the shrimp, endorsing the flavors while admitting she prefers the coconut rice. Michael closes the episode wishing viewers a happy Memorial Day and reminding them to keep things simple and delicious.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: Michael Symon grills a spatchcock chicken with avgolemono sauce in his Venice Beach front yard, joined by his wife Liz and co-host Liv. The episode features a lavender lemon drop martini and explores grill techniques for perfectly crispy, juicy poultry.

programme.title: Chewed Up
programme.desc: In this Halloween-themed episode, Carla Hall assumes the role of Queen of Halloween and welcomes Clinton Kelly and Michael Symon for a spooky celebration. Guest Jeanette Donnarumma returns to demonstrate crafty crescent roll appetizers including coffin pizza pockets, mummy dogs wrapped in crescent dough, and spider bites. The hosts also create Halloween mocktails like the Purple Potion Punch and HALL-o-Ween Hot Honey Punch. The Crafty Lumberjacks join to showcase easy party crafts including pumpkin photo frames, witch wine bottles, glue gun candelabras, temporary tattoo candles, and pumpkins wrapped in festive tights. Recipes featured include Pumpkin Cheesecake Crescent Moons and various appetizers perfect for Halloween gatherings.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: In this episode of Simply Symons, hosts Michael Symon and Liz Symon, joined by Liv Annacone, bring the show indoors to cook during warm weather. Michael creates an elevated crab grilled cheese sandwich using mascarpone, jumbo lump crab meat, Old Bay seasoning, tarragon mustard, and pickled red onions, with parmigiano-reggiano crust for extra crispness. Meanwhile, Liz prepares an orange whip cocktail with a modern twist, substituting tangerine juice for traditional orange juice and combining vodka, rum, Grand Marnier, and heavy cream. The episode showcases kitchen techniques like gentle folding to preserve crab lumps and discusses alternative grilled cheese fillings, while celebrating nostalgic Cleveland dining memories and mall culture.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: On Father's Day, Michael Symon prepares his ideal meal featuring a dry-aged prime ribeye steak seasoned with beef tallow, kosher salt, and pepper, grilled to a perfect char. He creates a vibrant salsa verde with anchovies, capers, fresh herbs (tarragon, parsley, mint), and red wine vinegar to complement the rich beef. Liz Symon crafts an equal-parts cocktail combining bourbon, amaro, and blood orange juice with cold brew coffee, garnished with a blood orange peel and crunchy salt. Michael also grills bitter endive with olive oil and finishes plates with orange segments. Throughout, the hosts discuss beef tallow versus olive oil, charcoal selection, proper salt techniques, and how the steak's varying fat content creates different doneness levels across a single cut.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: For the Fourth of July, Michael Symon showcases his approach to smoked ribs, starting with a custom cherry BBQ sauce made from cherry juice, sherry vinegar, molasses, bourbon, cold brew coffee, and warm spices. He explains his smoking technique at 300-325°F for two and a half hours, finishing the ribs on the grill for char and caramelization. Meanwhile, Liz Symon prepares a tart cherry Negroni—an equal-parts cocktail featuring gin, Campari, sweet vermouth, tart cherry juice, and a splash of seltzer. The episode balances savory and sweet as the hosts discuss rib texture preferences, ideal side dishes, and the versatility of the cherry sauce.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: On Simply Symons, Michael Symon, his wife Liz, and Liv Annacone cook Big Rigs rigatoni with spicy Italian sausage and vodka sauce in their front yard. Michael demonstrates his "cheater sauce" approach using pre-seasoned sausage, tomato paste, cream, and vodka that comes together in under 30 minutes without needing a knife. The hosts discuss pasta cooking techniques, the importance of finishing pasta in sauce rather than plating separately, proper seasoning of pasta water, and using quality ingredients like whole Parmigiano-Reggiano. They pair the dish with Lambrusco, an Italian sparkling red wine, exploring its versatility with various cuisines and its ability to cut through rich, spicy flavors.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: On Simply Symons, Michael Symon demonstrates how to properly grill skirt steak, explaining the differences between skirt and flank cuts and the importance of cutting against the grain. He seasons the thin-cut steak with salt, pepper, soy sauce, and Dijon mustard for extra caramelization, cooking it quickly over high heat to achieve a perfect medium-rare. Meanwhile, Liz Symon builds a vibrant chopped salad featuring romaine and butter lettuce, cherry tomatoes, red onion, fresh dill, and blue cheese, dressed with a homemade red wine vinaigrette shaken in a mason jar. Liz also creates a Martinez cocktail—a stirred drink combining vodka, sweet vermouth, bitters, and amarena cherry juice—which she describes as a cross between a vodka martini and an old fashioned. The hosts discuss lettuce varieties, proper salad dressing ratios, and why steak pairs better with textured, acidic sides than with starches.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: In this episode of Simply Symons, Michael Symon grills single-bone pork chops over hot coals and pairs them with a flavorful broth-based sauce of sautéed banana peppers, sweet red peppers, garlic, red onion, chili flakes, Dijon mustard, and herbs. Liz Symon demonstrates how to make a bourbon maple lemonade cocktail with fresh lemon juice and maple simple syrup, ideal for summer entertaining. Co-host Liv Annacone joins the banter as the hosts discuss seasoning techniques, grill setup, and the importance of honest communication in relationships while preparing and finishing this vibrant, quick-cooking American-Italian dish.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: On Simply Symons, hosts Michael and Liz Symon welcome Liv Annacone to their Venice bay home where they celebrate summer clamming season. Michael prepares a classic steamed clam dish featuring pancetta, garlic, shallots, chili flakes, and white wine, served with grilled sourdough bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato. Liz creates a French gimlet cocktail using vodka, fresh lime juice, and elderflower liqueur instead of traditional simple syrup. The hosts discuss clamming techniques, bread storage debate, herb preparation, and garlic preferences while encouraging Liv to expand her seafood palate with the briny, flavorful dish.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: On Simply Symons, Michael Symon creates a quick and inexpensive curry mussels dish featuring full-fat coconut milk, lime juice, cilantro, and fresh jalapenos, served with charred sourdough bread for soaking up the aromatic broth. Meanwhile, Liz Symon whips up fresas con crema, a deceptively simple dessert made with sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and crème fraîche, topped with fresh strawberries and finished with a hint of lime zest and mint. Host Liv Annacone tastes both dishes, and the hosts discuss the ease and elegance of preparing gourmet meals in minutes with minimal ingredients and prep work.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: Simply Symons hosts an upscale backyard tailgate featuring two main components: Michael's beer-poached bratwurst with kimchi, served on buttered and grilled hard rolls with pop mustard and optional Kewpie mayo, and Liz's inventive bourbon sour cocktail made with sage-infused bourbon, Benedictine, brown sugar simple syrup, lemon juice, lemon curd, and egg whites shaken in a mason jar. The hosts discuss bread storage methods, the classification of hot dogs as sandwiches, and bratwurst preparation techniques including splitting the sausage for better presentation. Liv joins in tasting both dishes, initially skeptical of kimchi but warming to the combination with Kewpie mayo and the bourbon sour despite typically avoiding bourbon.

programme.title: Ying Cooks the Internet
programme.desc: "Silky Spicy Eggplant" - Chris is joined by beloved cookbook author Hetty McKinnon to test out “EASY QUICK VEGAN EGGLANT RECIPE IN CHINA” from TikTok/IG sensation @foodiechina888 (a.k.a. Wayne Shen).

programme.title: Ying Cooks the Internet
programme.desc: "The ONE Pancake" - Chris tackles the fourth most Googled recipe of 2022: "Quick Pancake." His solution? THE ONE PANCAKE. Every ingredient is reduced to a unit of one (1 cup or 1 teaspoon), hence, THE ONE. It's literally an unforgettable recipe for delicious, and, most importantly, quick pancakes.

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime - Whole Roasted Chicken with Morgan McGlone: Our friend Morgan McGlone has cooked a lot of chicken—or "chook," as they call it in Australia, where he's from. He's a hell of a chef and restaurateur, as well as an excellent father to his son, Ryo. In this episode, he talks us through his roast chicken method, which, spoiler alert, involves a lot of butter. This is a bit of a long cook, so it's more of a weekend dish, but nothing beats breaking into a whole chicken with your family. The kids get to see food in its whole form, and pick the pices they want. The only decision you have to make is whether to share the best bits, or save them for yourself.

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime - Cantonese-Style Steamed Fish with Morgan McGlone: World-class Australian chef Morgan McGlone joins Chris Ying to share his go-to technique for preparing a whole steamed fish—something his son absolutely loves! A lot of people are intimidated by cooking a whole fish, but this is our plea to you to get your kids started on steaming/eating whole fish early in life!

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime - Japanese Curry Your Kids (and You!) Will Love: Chris Ying shares his recipe for a creamy, dreamy Japanese curry that uses milk and honey to hit all the right notes that kids love. If your kids already like curry...you're golden with this recipe! And if your kids are new to the curry game, this is the perfect introduction.

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime: Hacky Pad Thai for the Whole Family - This... is not pad thai. It has everything you love about pad thai—umami, sweetness, chewy rice noodles, brightness from lime—but this is the super hacky version I make for my wife and kids whenever I come across a package of fresh or semi-fresh noodles at the Asian market. If one of my Thai friends comes over, I'm hiding this from them. (If you're watching this, I'm sorry. It's all in the name of feeding the kids!) Ingredient-wise, you can keep tamarind and fish sauce in the fridge and pork belly in the freezer, but this recipe really depends on whether or not you have the noodles, which aren't available everywhere. You can use the dried kind, but I don't prefer them because they never seem to get to the right texture.

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime: Quick Chicken Piccata - So far, my kids have always happily eaten this chicken piccata. It's crispy, sweet, sour, and super savory thanks to those little capers (which are easy to pluck out if the kids don't want them). But the real win is that my wife is obsessed with this dish, too. Usually, I can have this on the table in under 25 minutes, start to finish, which is a huge win. Also, while I almost always prefer chicken thighs, this is one of the rare instances where white meat is just fine.

programme.title: Winning Mealtime
programme.desc: Winning Mealtime: Sweet Sour Pork Ribs (aka "Kid McGear Bones") - Chris makes a go-to favorite for his kids—sticky, sweet and sour pork ribs in bite-sized portions.

programme.title: Recipe Lab with Chris Ying
programme.desc: "Redemption Rice" - After an ill-advised dalliance with a terrible chicken korma recipe, Chris tries to redeem the category of mixed-rice dishes, starting with the classic Japanese Takikomi Gohan.

programme.title: Recipe Lab with Chris Ying
programme.desc: "Jungle Bird and Compari Sun" - It’s been a long week in the studio. Chris wraps up his night by demonstrating the only two cocktail recipes he knows: the Jungle Bird and the Campari Sun.

programme.title: Recipe Lab with Chris Ying
programme.desc: "Crispy Gnocchi with Burst Tomatoes" - Chris prepares one of the all-time most popular dishes from New York Times Cooking: Crispy Gnocchi with Burst Tomatoes. Tune in to see if the dish lives up to its poetic name.

programme.title: Recipe Lab with Chris Ying
programme.desc: "Fluff Bread" - According to TikTok, egg whites + sugar + cornstarch + chocolate chips = cloud (a.k.a.) fluff bread. In this episode, Chris checks the math on this equation.

programme.title: Recipe Lab with Chris Ying
programme.desc: "Crispy Pork Belly" - Inspired by something he saw on TikTok, Chris faces his fears and begins working on a dish hes never successfully gotten right: crispy, Cantonese-style roast pork belly.

programme.title: Ellie's Real Good Food
programme.desc: The key to having chocolate in your life in a manageable way is to go for quality over quantity. Recipes include Fig Ginger Truffles, Double-Chocolate Waffles a la Mode, Mocha Java Smoothie, and more.

Recipes include Whole Grain Penne with Chicken, Mushrooms Spinach, Basil Pesto with Spaghetti Squash, and more.

programme.title: Ellie's Real Good Food
programme.desc: We all love cheese--who doesn't? But there can be too much of a good thing. Ellie answers an SOS from a home where cheese has completely taken over the menu. Ellie, a cheese lover herself, shows how to keep from going overboard with cheese and instead utilize its best assets—its great flavor and health benefits. Recipes include Skillet Mac and Cheese, Parmesan-crusted Chicken Breast, and more.

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why is there a giant hole in the top of the Pantheon? And how is it still standing after more than two millennia? Why does Piazza Navona look like a racetrack? And why did it used to be a swimming pool? Where did the bronze for St. Peter's Basilica come from, and why are those windows in the dome so heavenly?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why did Shakespeare use Kronborg Castle as the setting for Hamlet? Was picturesque Nyhavn really the playground for sailors and brothels? Christiansborg Palace, Amalienborg Palace, Rosenborg Palace - why so many palaces in one small European country?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Who was Gassy Jack why was he so gassy? Why was Capilano Bridge built and what do all those totem poles mean? What's so important about the Hotel Vancouver, and what does it have to do with the train station, the Queen of England, and Harry Potter? Who was Yip Sang, and why did he have his own Boy Scout Troop?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: When and why were so many stunning chteaux built in such a concentrated area in central France? Why is there a river running through Chteau de Chenonceau, and what do the ladies of the castle have to do with it? Why does Chteau de Chambord have 440 rooms, yet no one ever lived there? Why is there a porcupine over the entrance to Chteau d'Amboise?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Where is the hidden symbol of Venice on the iconic gondola? Why are there two different saints on the gateway columns? Why is the solar system off on Torre dell'Orologio? Why does Saint Mark's Basilica look like Hagia Sophia? Why does the Doge's Palace have a Stairway of Giants, and what do those symbols mean?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why is there a beautiful, tiny blue-domed church floating in Kotorska Bay? Why did someone build 1350 steps up the side of Kotor's mountain? Why is the Cathedral of Saint Tryphon pink? And why are the towers mismatched? Why are the streets within the fortress walls intentionally in a maze?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why are you encouraged to walk on the rooftop of the Oslo Opera House? Why did Vikings live here, and why are their ships shaped like that? Why was the Oslo National Theatre built, and what's that secret staircase? What is the troll legend, and why did it happen here?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Who got hitched at Bordeaux Cathedral and why was it such an important moment in history? Did Parisian architecture actually come from Bordeaux? Why is Bordeaux so synonymous with wine? What was the Place de la Bourse hiding? What do all these sculptures mean at Place des Quinconces? Why were two ancient gates spared?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why did ancient Roman rich famous choose to vacation here? Who opened the gate for the bad guys in the 1500s? What does the town clock tower symbolize? What's the history of majolica tile art? Why are Sorrento lemons and limoncello so famous?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: What did Alfred Nobel invent that led him to create the Nobel Prize? What is Gamla Stan? What's so important about the throne inside the Royal Palace of Stockholm? What is the Djurgrden Canal, and why was it only for the Royal Family? Why did the Swedes grow grass on their rooftops, and what's the history of their folk costumes?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why did the famous French architect Viollet-le-Duc only work on one residence: the historic Roquetaillade Castle? Why is there a monolithic church in St. Emilion? And why did its monk sleep underground? Why is there a giant wall around the tiny village of Blaye? And why was beautiful Bourg-en-Gironde built into the side of a cliff? And how do Cadillac and Pauillac make time stand still?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: How did Dublin get its name? And what do Vikings and a black pool have to do with it? Who was Maewyn Succat, and why is he celebrated with green beer? How did the harp become a symbol of Ireland, and why do the harps on Irish coins and Guinness beer look different? What is the curious history of the Book of Kells, and how did it make its way into Trinity Colleges Longroom Library?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Who were the Habsburgs, Maria Theresa, Franz Joseph and Sisi? And how did they shape Vienna? What is the Ringstrasse, and why are there so many oversized, ornate public buildings dotting it? Where did Mozart perform as a 6-year-old prodigy? When and why did Austria shrink to a tenth of its size? What do the eagles on the rooftop of St. Stephens Cathedral symbolize? And why are Viennas coffee and pastries so legendary?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: This beautiful region of England is full of picture-perfect rolling hills, quaint stone cottages, sprawling country estates and that distinct Yorkshire dialect. Why are country estates named Castles and Abbeys? What is The Shambles, and how did it get its name? Why is one of the largest medieval Gothic cathedrals in Europe in the small town of York? How did the Quakers and chocolate shape Yorks history? Where and what is Herriots country?

programme.title: Curious Traveler
programme.desc: Why is there a giant church complex, the DomQuartier, in this tiny Alpine town? And why is there an equally giant medieval fortress high above it? Who lived in Mirabell Palace? And Hellbrun Palace? Why is Getreidegassse so charming, and why are those shop signs so important? And how do you solve a problem like Maria? From the Sound of Music to Silent Night to the Sonatas of this towns beloved Mozart, its time to get curious about Salzburg.

programme.title: Mikkie & Dale
programme.desc: Die Unternehmerin Mikkie fing vor einem Jahr an, Dale zu daten und verliebte sich schnell in ihn. Sie träumt von der Ehe, hat aber noch nie Dales Familie kennengelernt. Werden Dales Gründe, Mikkie zu verstecken, die Beziehung zum Scheitern bringen?

programme.title: Allerlei Auberginen
programme.desc: Bevor sie sich einer intensiven Fruchtbarkeitsbehandlung unterzieht, will die misstrauische Star sichergehen, dass ihr viel jüngerer Freund Ricky ihr und ihrem zukünftigen Kind treu bleibt.

programme.title: Er machte uns beiden einen Heiratsantrag
programme.desc: Leila, ein Model aus der Schweiz, war hin und weg, als sie West vor vier Jahren kennenlernte. Aber in letzter Zeit hat sich West anders verhalten, weshalb Leila glaubt, dass ihr Traummann sie betrügen könnte.

programme.title: Das ist meine Ex-beste Freundin
programme.desc: Joe, Lexis Freund seit 5 Jahren, hat ihr bei ihrer Modelkarriere geholfen. Seit kurzem hat sie angefangen zu vermuten, dass Joe ein Auge auf eine andere Frau geworfen hat.

programme.title: Ich komme mir vor wie eine Affäre
programme.desc: Jessica dachte, ihre Beziehung mit ihrem Musiker-Freund wäre in perfekter Harmonie, bis sie argwöhnt, dass sein Verhältnis zu seiner besten Freundin bei ihm neue Töne anstimmt.

programme.title: Das Date
programme.desc: Matty lädt Jenna zu ihrem ersten richtigen Date ein. Aber eine Enthüllung führt dazu, dass Jenna ihre Romanze mit Matty komplett infrage stellt.

programme.title: Ballkönigin
programme.desc: Jenna hofft, dass Matty sie fragt, ob sie mit ihm zum Winterball geht, und Sadie verdirbt Jennas Nominierung als Ballkönigin.

programme.title: Ich bin Jenna Hamilton
programme.desc: Jenna muss sich endgültig zwischen Jake und Matty entscheiden. Tamaras Liebesleben nimmt eine überraschende Wende, Ming kommt mit einem unerwarteten Date, und das Geheimnis des anonymen Briefes wird gelüftet.

programme.title: Entscheidungen
programme.desc: Criscilla Anderson übt mit den Kandidatinnen eine für L.A. typische Choreo ein und gibt ihnen wertvolle Lebenstipps. Der Choreograf und Emmy-Gewinner Travis Wall hilft Kelli und Judy bei ein paar schwierigen Entscheidungen.

programme.title: Show Group
programme.desc: Die Kandidatinnen tanzen für die Show Group vor, um einen der begehrten Plätze zu ergattern. Fünf Kandidatinnen müssen noch gehen, und manche stechen negativ hervor.

programme.title: Augenblicke im Vorbeigehen I Tag 169 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Manche Momente entstehen ganz nebenbei. Tag 169 zeigt das tägliche Miteinander im Haus: mit kurzen Begegnungen, Blicken und kleinen Szenen, die den Tag prägen.

programme.title: Zwischen Tür und Alltag I Tag 170 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Auch an Tag 170 wird der Alltag im Haus begleitet. Was passiert zwischen Aufstehen, Essen, Reden und Warten? Die Folge zeigt das Haus in seiner gewohnten Unmittelbarkeit.

programme.title: Stillstand oder Bewegung? I Tag 171 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Wie fühlt sich Tag 171 im Haus an? Gibt es Veränderungen oder bleibt alles beim Alten? Die Kameras zeigen, wie der Tag verläuft – beobachtend, unkommentiert, nah dran.

programme.title: Ein Fenster in den Alltag I Tag 172 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Die Folge zu Tag 172 öffnet wieder ein Fenster in den Alltag im Big Brother Haus. Was wird sichtbar? Gespräche, Abläufe und Beobachtungen in gewohnt direkter Form.

programme.title: Was passiert, passiert I Tag 173 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Der Alltag läuft, wie er läuft. Tag 173 zeigt erneut, was das Leben im Haus ausmacht – ob auffällig oder unscheinbar. Jede Szene erzählt ein Stück des Gesamtbilds.

programme.title: Einfach ein weiterer Tag I Tag 174 Staffel 5
programme.desc: Tag 174 ist da – ohne große Ansagen, aber mit vielen kleinen Momenten. Was davon hängen bleibt, zeigt die Folge. Alltag im Haus – direkt eingefangen, wie er passiert.

programme.title: Neue Kapitel werden aufgeschlagen I 26 Weekly Live Show Staffel 5
programme.desc: Wie hat sich die Woche entwickelt? Vielleicht haben sich neue Allianzen geformt oder es gab stille Momente. Forschen wir gemeinsam nach.

programme.title: Die Geissens
programme.desc: Carmen und Robert Geiss besuchen ein Pferderennen in Hongkong – natürlich inklusive Wetten. Ob Carmens Einsatz auf mehrere Pferde klug ist? Seit über 10 Jahren zeigt RTLZWEI das glamouröse Leben der Kult-Millionäre zwischen Luxusalltag und exklusiven Events weltweit. (S2 E04)

programme.title: XXL-Shopping​​ & Super-Nanny
programme.desc: Carmen und Robert Geiss sind auf Shoppingtour, denn für ihre Luxusimmobilien benötigen sie eine luxuriöse Einrichtung. Dabei wird natürlich nicht gespart! Währenddessen passt Nanny Nummer 30 auf Shania und Davina auf. Ob sie die beiden im Griff hat? (S2 E05)

programme.title: Carmens Nerven liegen blank!
programme.desc: Für geschäftliche Termine reist die ganze Familie Geiss nach Kroatien. Dort angekommen werden Carmens Nerven nicht nur einmal auf die Probe gestellt... (S2 E07)

programme.title: Shopping-Drama in Dubrovnik
programme.desc: Carmen und Robert Geiss sind geschäftlich in Kroatien unterwegs. Carmen kann Dubrovnik natürlich nicht verlassen, ohne vorher shoppen gewesen zu sein. Allerdings gestaltet sich das Ganze schwieriger als gedacht... (S2 E08)

programme.title: Formel-1-Rennen​ & das erste Mal Bus fahren
programme.desc: Die Geissens sind total im Freizeitstress! Wie jedes Jahr möchte Robert das Formel-1-Rennen in Monaco besuchen - das ist allerdings nicht der einzige Termin, der auf das Wochenende fällt. Bei so viel Stress muss er sogar das erste Mal Bus fahren. (S2 E09)

programme.title: Geburtstags-Stress & Große Überraschung
programme.desc: Die Geissens schmeißen eine Geburtstagsparty für Tochter Davina - dafür muss noch einiges vorbereitet werden und Carmen gerät in Stress. Um die Vorbereitungen zu erleichtern, hat sie einen Überraschungsgast organisiert. (S2 E10)

programme.title: Schock bei den Geissens:​ Wird die Villa Geissini
programme.desc: Carmen Geiss freut sich auf eine entspannte und ruhige Familienzeit in der Villa Geissini in Saint-Tropez. Allerdings erhält Robert einen Anruf, der die ganze Planung durcheinanderbringt - ein Investor möchte die Villa kaufen... (S2 E11)

programme.title: Robert raubt Carmens letzten Nerv!
programme.desc: Carmen Geiss ist total genervt von ihrem Mann Robert. Erst hat er kein Verständnis für ihren Schuh-Tick und dann landet sie auch noch unfreiwillig im Pool... (S2 E12)

programme.title: Horror-Crash! Geiss-Töchter in Lebensgefahr?!
programme.desc: Damit hat niemand gerechnet! Opa Reinhold Geiss kommt mit dem Auto von der Straße ab - mit Davina und Shania Geiss auf dem Rücksitz! In der Not springt Davina sogar aus dem Auto... (S2 E13)

programme.title: Großer Musikvideo-Dreh: Robert ist genervt!
programme.desc: Carmen Geiss steht ein großer Tag bevor: Ihr erstes Musikvideo wird gedreht! Doch es läuft nicht wie geplant... Carmen hängt im Zeitplan total hinterher und Robert ist genervt. Ob der Drehtag am Ende noch erfolgreich wird? (S3 E02)

programme.title: Familie Geiss auf Adventure-Tour!
programme.desc: So hat sich Carmen den Urlaub aber nicht vorgestellt! Statt in Ruhe durch die Stadt zu schlendern, dürstet es Robert und die Kinder nach Action! (S3 E03)

programme.title: Carmen Geiss im Stress! Shanias Geburtstag steht vor
programme.desc: Ab geht die Post! Es ist viel los in der Villa Geissini. Immerhin wird der Geburtstag von Töchterchen Shania Geiss gefeiert! Die ersten Gäste sind schon da. Eins ist sicher: Die Partys werden von Jahr zu Jahr immer verrückter... (S3 E06)

programme.title: Das Jetset-Leben! Solo-Auftritt und eine Menge
programme.desc: Carmen Geiss hat am Abend ihren ersten Solo-Auftritt! Während sie ahnungslos beim Friseur sitzt, reist Robert Geiss zum Fußballstadion nach Hamburg. Kurz vor dem Auftritt liegen die Nerven von Carmen blank... (S3 E08)

programme.title: Butter bei die Fische: Das Saint-Tropez des Nordens!
programme.desc: Urlaub auf Sylt! Ganz nach Robert Geiss' Geschmack! Statt Wellenesstrip gibt es wieder pure Action! Wer braucht schon Erholung? Vom Fischkutter mit Austern-Tasting bis hin zum Rasen beim Offroad-Fahren am Strand ist alles dabei. (S3 E09)

programme.title: Tach Berlin! Sightseeing-Tour der Superlative!
programme.desc: Robert und Carmen Geiss erobern die Hauptstadt! Auf der Sightseeing-Tour durch Berlin wird ein neuer Schlitten auf eine etwas andere Art getestet. Ein kurzer Stopp bei Curry 36 darf nicht fehlen! (S3 E09)

programme.title: Viva Las Vegas: Liebe, Luxus und eine zweite Hochzeit?
programme.desc: Carmen und Robert Geiss kommen aus dem Staunen nicht mehr heraus. Ihre "Bleibe"? Ein wahrer Palast! Da fehlen sogar Carmen die Worte. Im Caesars Palace residieren sie als VIPs in einer luxuriösen Villa mit Privataufzug und Butler. (S3 E12)

programme.title: Alles auf die 20?! Robert Geiss spielt Roulette...
programme.desc: Pure Eskalation in Las Vegas! Die Geissens zocken im Casino mit 20k! Doch die Kugel rollt anders als gewollt. Aber dann geschieht ein Wunder! Robert Geiss kassiert einen richtig fetten Gewinn! (S3 E15)

programme.title: Pure Action! Familientrip in die Universal Studios!
programme.desc: Die Geissens sind zu Besuch in den Universal Studios. Hinter die Kulissen von Hollywood schauen? Kein Problem! Explosionen, Erdbeben und Fluten: Hier wird nicht an Special Effects gespart! (S3 E17)

programme.title: Oldtimer-Spritztour: Robert Geiss findet die Bremse
programme.desc: Carmen und Robert Geiss suchen in den USA nach Inspiration für eigene Bauprojekte. Carmen ist begeistert von den Ideen. Robert zeigt eher wenig Begeisterung... Jetzt hilft nur noch eins: eine Spritztour! Aber wo sind eigentlich die Bremsen? (S3 E18)

programme.title: PS-Spektakel: 🏎️ Robert Geiss auf der
programme.desc: Für Robert heißt es: Rasen, was das Zeug hält. Denn in Ischgl hat er ein klares Ziel vor Augen. Er will seine beste Rundenzeit auf der Kartbahn knacken! Doch das ist eine echte Herausforderung... Für Robert wird's so richtig anstrengend. (S3 E18)

programme.title: Mega-Fail in Monaco: Bierdusche für Carmen Geiss!
programme.desc: Formel-1-Wochenende in Monaco, und natürlich wird nichts dem Zufall überlassen! Von der Luxus-Terrasse bis zum Sternekoch - hier wurde an alles gedacht! Doch plötzlich passiert's: Carmen Geiss kriegt unfreiwillig eine "Bierdusche" ab! (S3 E18)

programme.title: Letzter Stopp: San Francisco! Nachts allein in
programme.desc: In San Francisco angekommen, erkunden Robert und Carmen Geiss die Golden Gate Bridge! Als Abschluss ihrer USA-Reise gibt es noch eine private Führung im berühmtesten Gefängnis der Welt: Alcatraz! Allerdings kriegt Carmen richtig Muffensausen.. (S3 E19)

programme.title: Ohne Fleiß
programme.sub-title: kein Preis: Carmen Geiss' Kampf gegen
programme.desc: Carmen Geiss hat ihr Ziel vor Augen: Fünf Kilo abnehmen. Nach anderthalb Stunden Workout ist die ehemalige Miss Fitness auch fix und fertig - aber glücklich! (S3 E20)

programme.title: Ein Rennen gegen die Zeit: Speed-Shopping in Cannes!
programme.desc: Kaum in Cannes angekommen, beginnt Carmen Geiss mit ihrer Jagd nach Schuhen! Immerhin gibt es im Ausverkauf satte 50 Prozent Rabatt! Da muss sie einfach zuschlagen! (S4 E01)

programme.title: Ciao Milano! Familie Geiss auf Erkundungstour...
programme.desc: Die Geissens erkunden Mailand, vom Dom bis zur Leonardo-Statue. Carmen führt die Familie, während die kranke Davina mit den Großeltern ins Hotel zurückkehrt. Shania genießt die Zeit mit den Eltern, inklusive Juwelierbesuch. (S4 E02)

programme.title: Ganz nach Carmens Geschmack: Sixpack-Alarm in Miami!
programme.desc: Hot, hotter, South Beach! Hier jagt ein heißer Sixpack den nächsten! Carmen Geiss kommt aus dem Staunen gar nicht mehr heraus! Die "Beach Boys" haben es ihr so richtig angetan. (S4 E04)

programme.title: "Rakete auf dem Wasser!" Action-Urlaub in Miami...
programme.desc: Jetzt geht es mit Vollspeed über Miamis Küstengewässer. Doch nicht jedem gefallen 150 km/h so gut wie Robert Geiss… Denn Ehefrau Carmen bekommt Panik. (S4 E05)

programme.title: Davina Geiss' Schumacher- Fahrtraining
programme.desc: Davina bekommt zu ihrem 18. Geburtstag ihr erstes Auto geschenkt. Damit sie lernt, mit 450 PS zu hantieren, geht's direkt zum Fahrsicherheitstraining mit keinem anderen als Rennfahrerlegende Ralf Schumacher & Sohnemann. (S20 E22)

programme.title: Spritzen-Horror für Robert Geiss
programme.desc: Robert hat Schmerzen in seiner Ferse, hier muss was passieren! Doch wenn Spritzen ausgepackt werden, braucht Robert seine Carmen zum Händchenhalten. Wird er die Behandlung unbeschadet überstehen und kann den ersten Urlaubstag doch noch genießen? (S20 E23)

programme.title: Teens Spend 24 Hours in Haunted House
programme.desc: Pranksters Blake and Frank fake paranormal videos to go viral. Their teacher and classmates team up to flip the script, terrifying the duo in a "haunted" house to teach them a haunting lesson.

programme.title: Girls Get Revenge Against Mean Cheerleader
programme.desc: Mean girl Samantha, obsessed with perfection, gets a magic cream that turns her beautiful facade hideous. Humiliated and abandoned, she learns a harsh lesson about inner beauty, prompting a transformation that earns her genuine friendships.

programme.title: She Takes the Worst Job in the World
programme.desc: Ambitious lawyer Rachel joins a prestigious all-female firm, choosing wealth over family. She soon discovers her bosses are a literal witch coven using dark magic to win cases and steal her youth.

programme.title: Principal Bans Halloween Inside School
programme.desc: Rebellious student Rosa pranks Principal Danvers for banning Halloween, only to discover the ban stems from a tragic family fire. Rosa leads a movement to apologize and restore the holiday spirit.

programme.title: Bullied Kid Forced to Do Jocks Homework
programme.desc: Shy Henry discovers his new neighbor Frank is a werewolf. Rather than fleeing, Henry uses silver to help Frank control his curse. Their families bond as Frank's dad offers Henry's mom therapy.

programme.title: Best Friends Becomes Rivals
programme.desc: Carly, a hardworking student, pushes herself to the brink to honor a promise to her late father: a full scholarship to Berkeley. Overwhelmed by academic, athletic, and financial stress, she learns to prioritize her well-being, ultimately finding success and happiness.

programme.title: Girl Uses Trash for Halloween Decorations
programme.desc: Sweet, modest Gabby enters a Halloween decorating contest to win $2500. Despite bullying from wealthy Tiffany, Gabby uses trash and recycled items to create a masterpiece, proving resourcefulness wins.

programme.title: Kid on the Run Saved by Hero Neighbor
programme.desc: Matt, a veteran haunted by PTSD, finds redemption by befriending his young neighbor, Hailey. After saving her family from her abusive father, he finally finds the happiness and peace he deserves.

programme.title: Kid Gets Shocking Birthday Gift
programme.desc: To avoid expensive last-minute flights, cheapskate Owen tries to ship himself in a box to his brother's birthday. A shipping error sends him to Florida instead of California, costing him a fortune.

programme.title: Teen Secretly Swaps Designer Bags for Fakes
programme.desc: When teen influencer Bridget is publicly exposed for carrying fake designer bags, her investigation reveals her best friend Yuna secretly swapped them to help her broke mother cover debts.

programme.title: Teen Shamed for Eating at Food Bank
programme.desc: When spoiled teen Madison shames classmate Camila for eating at a soup kitchen, her parents fake a financial crisis to teach her a lesson, leading to genuine friendship and unexpected salvation for Camila's family store.

programme.title: Middle Child Gets Ignored by Her Family
programme.desc: Overlooked middle triplet June exposes her family's superficial obsession with her sisters via an anonymous account, leading to her exile—before her writing talent earns her total independence and success.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Frau Weber ist eine stets schlecht gelaunte Angestellte im Arbeitsamt. Ein besonders schwer vermittelbarer Fall raubt ihr nun den letzten Nerv: ein gewisser Herr Tarzan mit fragwürdigen Qualifikationen lässt sich partout nicht wieder in Arbeit bringen.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: E-Mail-Kettenbriefe sollte man nicht einfach löschen. Vielleicht steht irgendwann Bettina Merten vor der Tür – bekannt aus dem Internet und mit einem Koffer mit 100.000 EUR in der Hand. Außerdem: Obdachlose verkaufen Diamanten für 24 Millionen Euro.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Carmen arbeitet in einem Tattoo-Shop und bleibt immer schön cool. Ob empörte Mütter, die sich über missglückte Piercings für ihre 6jährige Tochter aufregen oder Rocker, die auf dem Rücken ein Uschi-Glas-Tattoo wollen: für Carmen ist der Kunde König!

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Wer kennt das nicht: Auf einer Party trifft man jemanden, der einen zu kennen scheint. Und der einem mir nichts, dir nichts sein Herz ausschüttet. Aber wer in Gottes Namen ist das nur? Aus solchen Situationen entstehen gern besonders peinliche Momente.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Petra und Leo sind Rettungsschwimmer mit politischem Auftrag. Um gerettet zu werden, müssen sie FDP wählen. Wer sich weigert und untergeht macht damit klar: die Politikverdrossenheit in Deutschland greift um sich.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Filmproduzent Rolf Brunner, seine Assistentin Karin Maybach und Castingchef Detlev Harm bei einer Krisensitzung: Für die anstehende internationale Kinofilmproduktion findet sich kein Regisseur. Von Wedel bis Dietl – niemand ist abkömmlich …

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Die Gastgeber Britta und Stefan freuen sich über einen bisher gelungenen Silvesterabend mit Freunden. Als es ums Teilen der Kosten für die fröhliche Pärchenparty geht, schlägt die Stimmung jäh um: sooo viele Garnelen haben die einen gar nicht gegessen …

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Tina lässt sich im Computerladen von Verkäufer Frank beraten. Er empfiehlt die „saugeile“ Grafikkarte. Oder – wenn sie auf Nummer sicher gehen will – eine „hammergeile“. Die wäre dann sowohl für „dies und das“ als auch für „alles Mögliche“ geeignet.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Arbeitsalltag im Großraumbüro: Birte will um ein Uhr in die Mittagspause und fragt in die Runde, ob die Kollegen mitkommen, sich die Titten vergrößern lassen. Die Kollegen sind ehrlich bestürzt, denn einige von Ihnen waren bereits in der Mittagspause …

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Judith und die lebensgroße Ratte Rolf sitzen beim gemeinsamen Essen im Restaurant. Der Kellner bietet als Dessert eine Käseplatte an, was Rolf als Diskriminierungsversuch deutet: „Käse? Weil ich ne Ratte bin, oder was?

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Die Badenixen Nina und Ute sonnen sich, als sie den Strandverkäufer Tom entdecken und heranwinken. Tom ist über und über mit Uhren, Hüten und weiteren Utensilien behängt. Im Gespräch stellt sich heraus, dass er gar nichts verkaufen möchte.

programme.title: Ladykracher
programme.desc: Die besten Sketche aus der vierten Staffel Ladykracher. Natürlich gibt es auch ein Wiedersehen mit der legendären Pimmelnase, dem vergesslichen Tätowierten und der Deutschstunde für Anfänger. Anke Engelke und das große Ladykracher-Special!

programme.title: Ladykracher

Ladykracher ist endlich zurück und wie gewohnt zündet Anke mit ihrem einzigartigen Ensemble wieder ein Feuerwerk an durchgeknallten Sketche ab.

programme.title: Lakshmis Haus des Schicksals
programme.desc: Lakshmi Niwas ist ein gefühlvolles Familiendrama, das in einem traditionellen Haushalt spielt, in dem Beziehungen, Werte und Schicksal eng miteinander verbunden sind. Lakshmi ist eine starke und mitfühlende Frau, die zur emotionalen Stütze einer Familie wird, die von Liebe getragen, aber von Konflikten, Erwartungen und dem Wandel der Zeit herausgefordert wird. Während Generationen aufeinandertreffen und verborgene Wahrheiten ans Licht kommen, muss Lakshmi zwischen Pflicht, Opferbereitschaft und persönlichem Glück ihren eigenen Weg finden. Die Serie erzählt von Vertrauen, Zusammenhalt und der Bedeutung von Familie – Themen, die universell verständlich sind. Lakshmi Niwas ist eine Geschichte über Hoffnung, emotionale Bindungen und die stille Stärke einer Frau, die aus einem Haus ein Zuhause macht.

programme.desc: Auf dem Wiederstein-Hof leben drei Generationen: Birgit führt das Weingut, ihr Mann Christian einen Gourmet-Landgasthof, die Mutter brennt Schnaps, der Vater ist Fachmann für Böden. Statt Standardware entwickelt Birgit mit dem australischen Weinberater Mac Forbes einen unverwechselbaren Stil bis hin zu Namen wie „Venus" oder „Diva".
